reason: The observation is true and the argument built on it is not, and the fix as written does nothing. TRUE: grep of lately.html returns zero ':active' rules, and .dot (a real <button>, line 620) computes cursor: default at 1440 while a.kpi, .tab and .btn compute pointer (measured in chromium: kpi=pointer, dot=default, tab=pointer, btn=pointer via line 358). FALSE, and it is the load-bearing half: 'under a coarse pointer the press is the only channel by which the surface can confirm a touch registered'. It is not. Lines 938-944 bind pointerdown on every [data-tip] mark and, for pointerType touch, raise a pinned tooltip naming the job on the down event itself; a second tap dismisses it and a tap elsewhere drops it. interaction-check.mjs proves all three at 390x844 with hasTouch ('a real touch on a mark names it', 'a second touch on the same mark dismisses it', 'a touch away from the marks dismisses it'). So tapping a mark and tapping 2px beside it are the opposite of identical — one raises a black tooltip with the job title, the other dismisses. The finding restates a channel the behaviour gate already proves, then asserts the reverse of what it proves. THE FIX IS INERT WHERE IT MATTERS MOST. .dot::before carries 'animation: pop ... both' (line 302) and @keyframes pop ends at 'transform: scale(1)' (line 405). With fill-mode both, the animation origin outranks author declarations forever, so '.dot:active::before { transform: scale(0.82) }' never renders. Measured by cloning the rule onto a class: plain transform:scale(0.82) computes matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0); only !important computes matrix(0.82,...). (The same cascade error already sits dead in this file at lines 421 and 427.) Second, independent kill: the touch branch calls e.preventDefault() on pointerdown (line 941), which suppresses the compatibility sequence and the activation behaviour that would apply :active on touch — so on the one pointer the finding argues for, the rule is doubly unreachable. The .tab number is also backwards: rest is --ink-3 #71717a and hover is --ink #111111, so :active at --ink-2 #3f3f46 makes a pressed tab LIGHTER than a hovered one, and lighter still than the aria-current tab it would also hit. And a.kpi's border jump is overstated: --line here is not #e4e4e7 but rgba(17,17,17,0.10), so going to solid --ink-4 #a1a1aa on press is roughly a 5x contrast jump on a card whose whole discipline is graded ink. SEVERITY IS OVERSTATED. 'defect = visibly wrong but passable' does not hold: nothing in any of the ten frames is wrong, every control has both a hover and a focus-visible state, and the touch channel is proven to confirm. What is left is genuine polish — a missing press channel and one missing cursor — which is refinement.
sharpenedFix: Keep two of the four, correct one, drop one, and fix the dot a different way. (1) cursor: pointer on .dot — the one uncontested line; it is a <button> and browsers give buttons cursor: default. (2) a.kpi:active { transform: translateY(0); } and nothing else — the press reads as the 2px lift being pushed back down, which is the whole gesture; leave border-color at hover's --line rather than jumping to solid --ink-4. (3) .btn:active { border-color: var(--ink-3); transform: translateY(1px); } — background already equals hover's --paper-3, so repeating it buys nothing; note .btn's transition list (line 359) omits transform, so the 1px is instant in both directions, which is correct for a press. (4) .dot: do NOT use transform on the pseudo. Either darken the token the disc already keys off — .dot:active { --disc: var(--ink-2); } (no cascade conflict; --disc is a background, not an animated property) — or, if a size change is wanted, use the independent transform property, .dot:active::before { scale: 0.9; }, which composes with the pop keyframes instead of losing to them (measured: computes scale:0.82 while transform stays identity). Even then, prove it on touch: with preventDefault on line 941 the :active state may never apply there, in which case the honest answer is that the dot's touch confirmation is the pinned tooltip, already shipped, and the press state is a desk-only refinement. (5) Drop .tab:active entirely, or set it to var(--ink) — --ink-2 inverts the hover ramp.
breaks: Nothing structural — all five are additive rules on existing tokens with no palette, weight or architecture change. What must be re-measured after it lands: interaction-check.mjs in full (the dot's touch path is the one it exercises hardest — tooltip pin, second-tap dismiss, tap-away dismiss at 390x844 with hasTouch; a --disc change on :active must not disturb the tooltip pin, and any :active rule on .dot must be verified not to fight the preventDefault path); audit.mjs for hit targets and motion (a.kpi:active returning to translateY(0) is inside the existing transition on transform, and the .dot fix must stay on the pseudo so the 28px hit floor the comment at line 296 guards is untouched — this is exactly the regression that comment records); and re-shoot the ten frames only if the settled snapshot moves, which it should not, since every added rule is user-state-gated and data-motion=settled photographs the surface at rest. Also confirm the dark theme: --ink-2 inverts to #d4d4d8 there, so a :active that darkens the disc in light must be checked to still read as a change against Ground, not as a wash-out.
